7.7 — Level Studio II + Cross-Playtest

Yesterday you built it; today strangers meet it. Polish the two beats that most need it, then run the cross-playtest — different partner, full cave, numbers on paper. This closes the level arc of the semester: next stop, the boss.

Studio Brief ~25 min

Polish pass — exactly two beats. From yesterday's walk ritual and written plan (7.6), you know which. Polish means:

  • Sightlines: trim tiles until the next beat is glimpsed from the current one
  • Telegraphing: the threat is visible at rest before it is a threat (turret seen, not surprise-shot)
  • Reward placement: coins on the route you WANT walked; the coin trail is a dotted line your player follows without noticing
  • Death audit fix: the beat where a death costs the most gets either a checkpoint trigger (build one — it is a tag + a stored position) or a shortened approach

Do NOT polish everything. Two beats, deeply. That is how studio time works under deadline — and your deadline is the cross-playtest starting in 20 minutes.

Bug Hunt: Pre-test ritual

  1. Full-walk one more time, naming beats. Any NEW seams from polishing? Tile edits move colliders — check the walls you nudged.
  2. Verify from spawn: does the player know where to go within 5 seconds WITHOUT any instruction? What tells them — write the exact visual cue.
Cross-Playtest ~25 min

New partner (not yesterday's). Silent watching (2.4 rules). Full cave, entrance to boss door. Record per BEAT, not per session — the beat is the unit of analysis (this table is the exact habit that becomes the dataset unit, 9.5):

BeatDeathsTimeTester said / didFix candidate
1 Entrance
2
3
4
5
6 Boss door

Then swap: you play THEIR cave with the same table. You are both designer and tester today — notice how different the jobs feel.

Tinker: Read the numbers

  1. Compare the two tables (yours-as-designer vs theirs-as-tester). One fix only, from THEIR data. Apply it now — re-run that beat with them once.
  2. Look at total deaths vs your 7.5 prediction. Was your difficulty curve right? Where did reality disagree?
  3. Commit + push: "7.7a: cross-playtest data + one fix" — the table goes in the repo.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Polish two beats deeply: sightline, telegraph, reward route
  • Run a beat-granular playtest and record deaths/time/quotes
  • Apply exactly one fix from tester data and re-verify
  • Compare your predicted difficulty curve to the measured one
